title: Adaptive heavy-hitter sampling and explainer playbooks for SLO fidelity
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We continue to see noisy burn-rate and tail-latency alerts caused by bursty traffic from a small set of heavy-hitter routes and tenants. Current uniform sampling in trace ingestion drops most of the diagnostic traces during bursts, making postmortems slow and leading to frequent false-positive page-outs.

Goal: Implement an adaptive sampling layer that automatically detects heavy hitters (routes/tenants/users) and increases trace retention and preferred metric resolution for those keys. Produce an automated 'explainer' artifact per alert (a short human-readable summary + suggested runbook steps) to reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA). Integrate sampling decisions with the metrics/log pipeline so burn-rate alerts evaluate on consistent signals and the oncall receives high-signal traces only when needed.

Scope: 
- Tracing hook changes in our runtime to tag candidate heavy-hitters and emit priority sampling keys.
- A lightweight heavy-hitter detector service (streamed sketches) in the telemetry ingestion path.
- Sampling policy engine that accepts dynamic rules from Console and service defaults.
- Metrics/log pipeline enhancement to raise resolution for tagged keys (shorter histogram buckets + denser metric pushes during bursts).
- Alert explainer generator: a lambda that runs when a burn-rate/anomaly alert fires and emits a compact summary (top routes, top error codes, representative span examples, suggested next steps).
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline detects heavy hitters with >80% precision and <10% extra retention overhead for normal traffic
When a burn-rate alert fires for a route, the explainer contains top-3 culprit spans and suggested runbook step
Sampling policy is editable in Console and takes effect within 30s of change
Oncall pages rate for SLOs fall by at least 25% in the first 30 days in A/B test cohort
No regressions in steady-state cost beyond +5% telemetry storage for annotated tenants
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfood on staging for 2 weeks (10% of traffic routed through detector). Phase 2: A/B test on three mid-size customers for 4 weeks measuring page volume and MTTA. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% with Console opt-out and per-tenant caps. Rollback: flip sampling-policy to 'uniform' and disable detector stream (takes effect within 30s).
test_plan: Unit tests for sketch ingest and eviction, integration tests for sampling tag propagation across runtime -> ingest -> storage, e2e test that fires synthetic burst and verifies explainer generation, load test to measure ingestion CPU and memory with detector enabled. Create canary dashboard for detection latency and false-positive rate.
updates: 2025-02-19: Kickoff sync with runtime, ingestion, and console teams. Agreed to use count-min sketch for initial detector. Assigned infra tickets for provisioning sketch cluster.

2025-02-24: Prototype tracing hook landed in runtime PR (see PR #2987). Hook annotates spans with sampling-key and preferred-retention TTL. Initial feedback from runtime: small memory overhead (~1.2MB per worker).

2025-02-28: Ingest sketch prototype validated on staging traffic. Detector identifies top-50 routes reliably but misclassifies a high-cardinality test tenant; added heuristic to require sustained >30s signal before raising retention.
2025-03-02: Explainer prototype (lambda) generated plausible summaries for synthetic burn-rate alerts. UX review requested from SRE & PM — need shorter language and direct runbook links.
2025-03-04: QA found a race in policy propagation when Console pushes bulk updates; mitigation plan: versioned policy stamps and apply-then-activate step. Working on fix in PR #4124.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full-fidelity sampling for all traces is too costly; per-tenant retention caps required to avoid storage blowups. We considered a machine-learning classifier for heavy hitters but deferred to streaming sketches due to complexity and explainability requirements. Long-term: evaluate integrating explainer with post-incident replay service and autosuggesting SLO changes when repeated explainers show recurring root causes.
